title: SIndustries v1 site
summary: The first public SIndustries website shipped with sections for signals, systems, stacks, ships, stories, studio work, and contact.
evidence: Live website refresh completed before the content-ops migration.

title: Bookmark archiver skill
summary: A workflow skill for turning saved signals into a more durable review and action pipeline.
evidence: Public homepage ships this as an existing release signal.

title: Weekly content review pipeline
summary: An automated workflow that collects daily ops notes, distils them into a weekly review file, and creates structured content tasks ready for authoring and publication to this website.
evidence: Pipeline shipped 2026-06-01: daily ops note capture runs on each heartbeat cycle, weekly cron produces the review file and downstream content tasks.

title: Content factory v1
summary: First full content cycle completed end-to-end: Quinn orchestrates, Ivy authors, Tom approves, and Lobster auto-merges. Signal to published content without manual coordination.
evidence: Full cycle completed 2026-06-04: content task created, Ivy PR authored, Tom review passed, Lobster merge executed.

title: Tasks history
summary: Task history shipped across the Tasks API, schema, and UI tab. Past task changes are now queryable and visible.
evidence: Tasks API gained history endpoints, the schema was migrated to support history, and the UI added a History tab.

title: Pencil design system
summary: Design-token pipeline and shared UI integration shipped. Colour and sync refinements followed on 2026-06-11.
evidence: Pencil design token library and token pipeline shipped 2026-06-09; tasks-app integrates @sindustries/ui; dark theme enabled. Colour refinements and sync consistency checks shipped 2026-06-11. As of 2026-06-19 the token pipeline feeds both production surfaces through shared `@sindustries/ui` primitives — the website and the tasks-app now render buttons, inputs, layouts, and tokens from the same source.

title: Bookmark-to-task pipeline
summary: Full X bookmark ingest-to-task pipeline shipped: bookmark review, spec authoring, markdown approval request, and task creation from approved specs.
evidence: Pipeline shipped 2026-06-17 with 110 tests across 53 files. The end-to-end loop — ingest, curate, spec, approve, create task — runs through a single heartbeat-driven workflow, with spec approvals routed via the OpenClaw gateway.

title: Linked article bookmark ingest
summary: Bookmark ingest now captures linked article bodies and quoted X article text so the downstream summary, spec, and task all see the underlying source.
evidence: Linked article extraction and quoted X article parsing shipped 2026-06-18. The bookmark summary now contains the original article body or the quoted X article text, giving curation and spec authoring a richer source to work from.

title: Weekly repo audit automation
summary: Scheduled audit cron writes a weekly repo-audit doc and opens an idempotent Tom-approval PR labelled `code-audit` against main.
evidence: Cron, runner, and skill shipped 2026-06-19. The audit prompt is vendored as a skill, the cron writes `codebases/sindustries/docs/repo-audits/<YYYY-Www>.md` and opens a labelled PR per ISO week. Re-runs update the existing branch instead of opening duplicates.

title: Bookmark pipeline dashboard
summary: Dashboard shipped for the bookmark-to-content pipeline, tracking review state, spec generation, and approvals in a single view.
evidence: Bookmark pipeline dashboard shipped 2026-06-10.

title: SIndustries UI shared library rollout
summary: The website and tasks app now consume shared SIndustries UI tokens and components from one source, so design work compounds across both product surfaces.
evidence: Shared @sindustries/ui primitives now serve the website and tasks app; the tasks app also ships a tokens specimen page, and Pencil token sync consolidates into the shared UI artifact.

title: Morning brief ops escalation
summary: The daily morning brief now surfaces blocked agent-layer incidents and Quinn ops findings from persistent operating state.
evidence: Morning brief workflow now reads persistent incident and ops state and escalates items that need Tom attention into the daily brief.

title: Budgeting mobile live-data MVP
summary: The NZ budgeting mobile build moved from concept to a live-data MVP with accounts, balances, alerts, transactions, spending breakdowns, and recategorisation.
evidence: Budget mobile phases shipped accounts and cards screens, inline balance alert setup, delete confirmation, spending breakdowns, category transactions, recategorisation, transaction detail sheets, and Akahu-backed live bank sync.

title: Bookmark tagger gateway route
summary: Bookmark enrichment now routes through the OpenClaw gateway and emits descriptive content tags instead of fallback review labels.
evidence: The X bookmark tagger now returns descriptive tags such as agent architecture and token optimisation after moving through the OpenClaw gateway provider route.

title: Feature Factory v2
summary: Agents can now take an approved spec and self-orchestrate it through ready → doing → acceptance → done without Tom or Quinn driving transitions by hand.
evidence: Feature task workflow shipped 2026-06-29 (PR #117). The lobster handles spec approval, tech design gates, PR tracking, QA verification, and system spec requirements as a fully automated orchestration loop.

title: Task dependency UI
summary: Tasks now express blocking relationships. The UI shows what blocks each task, supports add/remove with title validation, and lets you copy task IDs from cards.
evidence: Task dependency backend (PR #128) and dependency UI (PR #129) shipped 2026-06-27–29. First capability to run the full spec → factory pipeline end-to-end.

title: Task type filter and selector
summary: The tasks app now filters by type, edits type on existing cards, and exposes feature as a creatable task type.
evidence: Task type filter and editor shipped 2026-06-30 (PR #145), closing task 5dbf2967.

title: Fluid spec drift lifecycle
summary: Spec changes after approval no longer hard-block the pipeline. The lobster unchecks Tom's approval and posts an AC diff; after Tom re-checks, the spec is resynced automatically.
evidence: Shipped across PRs #161, #163, #165, and #167 (2026-07-01 to 2026-07-03). Drift detection unchecks the approval marker, posts AC diff comments, and the resync path rewrites the brain spec from the task description after Tom re-approves.

title: Mission Control shell MVP
summary: A persistent operating shell shipped with tabs for active work, saved-signal review, and flow metrics, giving the studio one place to see its core loops.
evidence: Mission Control shell MVP shipped 2026-07-05 with a persistent navigation shell and embedded operating surfaces for tasks, bookmarks, and flow metrics.

title: Mission Control bookmarks tab
summary: Saved-signal review moved into Mission Control with live KPIs, topic breakdowns, pending approvals, and recent state changes.
evidence: The Mission Control bookmarks tab shipped 2026-07-08, exposing saved-signal pipeline KPIs, topic breakdowns, pending approvals, and recent transitions.

title: Mission Control shell-owned theme
summary: Day/night mode moved to the Mission Control shell, so the preference now stays consistent across the workspace and embedded task views.
evidence: Shell-owned theme preference shipped 2026-07-10 with cross-tab and embedded task-view synchronisation.

title: Worktree cleanup after feature delivery
summary: Feature-delivery cleanup now removes matching task worktrees after merge, keeping the build environment tidy without manual follow-up.
evidence: Post-merge feature-task cleanup shipped 2026-07-10 and now removes matching task worktrees idempotently.

title: Task creation operating standard
summary: The task-creation standard now separates product acceptance from implementation evidence, making the workflow clearer for agents and reviewers.
evidence: Task creation guidance updated 2026-07-07 to use real task types and keep acceptance checkbox state reserved for QA/product approval.

title: GymTrack MVP
summary: A mobile-capable workout logging MVP shipped under the Stoffer umbrella, with authenticated workout and set tracking ready for live deployment once provisioning is complete.
evidence: GymTrack MVP shipped 2026-07-13 with Vite, React, Supabase auth, row-level-secured workout and set records, and iOS Safari support; live deploy is pending Supabase provisioning.

title: Content Scheduler
summary: Mission Control can now compose, approve, schedule, and publish X posts through a guarded one-per-day publishing loop.
evidence: Content Scheduler shipped 2026-07-16 with compose, approval, scheduling, and publishing gates inside Mission Control.

title: SIndustries tab in Mission Control
summary: The public SIndustries site now runs inside Mission Control as an operating-surface tab, keeping website review closer to the studio's daily workflow.
evidence: SIndustries tab shipped in Mission Control on 2026-07-13, embedding the public brand site in the operating shell.

title: Unified agent incident schema
summary: Quinn and Lox now share a validated incident-state contract, making agent-layer incident reporting more consistent across operating workflows.
evidence: Unified incident schema shipped 2026-07-12 with a shared JSON-Schema-validated state contract and parser for Quinn and Lox.
